speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation. To begin my assessment, please tell me your age and what specific symptoms you are experiencing besides the fever and confusion.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Your age and history of tics while taking haloperidol are concerning; does your altered mentation present as confusion, delirium, or hallucinations? Also, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or changes in your speech or movement since starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is clinically diagnostic for NMS.
